issue.body:
# Bug report

<!-- 

⚠️ We receive a lot of bug reports which have already been solved or discussed. If you are looking for help, please try these first:

- Docs: https://docs.supabase.com
- Discussions: https://github.com/supabase/supabase/discussions
- Discord: https://discord.supabase.com

Before opening a bug report, please verify the following: 

-->

- [X] I confirm this is a bug with Supabase, not with my own application. 
- [X] I confirm I have searched the [Docs](https://docs.supabase.com), GitHub [Discussions](https://github.com/supabase/supabase/discussions), and [Discord](https://discord.supabase.com). 

## Describe the bug

There is a navigation race condition in `apps/studio/components/interfaces/SignIn/SignInPartner.tsx` caused by an unguarded asynchronous operation inside a `useEffect`.

On mount, an IIFE is triggered to fetch `auth.getSession()` and potentially `auth.signInWithIdToken()`. If the user navigates away from this page (unmounting the component) before these network promises resolve, the `finally` or `else` blocks will still blindly execute `router.replace()`. This creates a ghost redirect that hijacks the user's session and yanks them away from whatever new page they navigated to.

## To Reproduce
Steps to reproduce the behavior:

1. Open your browser's network tab and throttle the speed to "Slow 3G" (to easily catch the race condition).
2. Navigate to the partner sign-in route with mock parameters (e.g., `/sign-in-partner?partner=foo&id_token=bar`).
3. While the `Loader2` is spinning, immediately click the browser's "Back" button or click a link to navigate away to a different dashboard page.
4. Wait a few seconds for the pending authentication promises to resolve in the background.
5. See error: You are forcefully redirected to `/sign-in-mfa` or `/sign-in`, overriding your explicit navigation.

## Expected behavior


The `useEffect` should respect the component lifecycle. If the component unmounts before the authentication promises resolve, the router should safely ignore the redirect commands to prevent pulling the user away from their current, active page.


## System information

* OS: macOS / Windows / Linux
* Browser: All browsers
* Context: Supabase Studio Dashboard (`apps/studio`)

## Additional context

This is a standard React lifecycle edge case. The fix requires adding a simple isMounted flag within the useEffect hook.

By setting let isMounted = true at the start of the effect and returning a cleanup function that sets isMounted = false, we can wrap the router.replace() calls in an if (isMounted) check. This acts as a guard, ensuring the router only triggers if the component is still actively rendered in the DOM.

Since this only touches the local lifecycle of SignInPartner.tsx, it is an isolated, low-risk frontend patch.

I have tested this fix locally and it completely resolves the ghost redirect. I have a branch ready and can open a PR for this immediately if approved.

+/**
+ * Recovery for failed lazy-loaded JS/CSS chunks (route chunks, `next/dynamic`,
+ * `React.lazy`, Monaco, …), which happen on flaky or mobile networks and after
+ * deploys that remove old chunks.
+ *
+ * A page reload is the only reliable recovery: WebKit caches a failed module
+ * fetch in the document's module map, so every later `import()` of the same
+ * URL fails instantly until the document is replaced.
+ */
+
+export const CHUNK_LOAD_RELOAD_STORAGE_KEY = 'supabase-studio:chunk-load-reload'
+
+/**
+ * Minimum time between two automatic reloads in the same tab. A chunk that
+ * fails again within this window after a reload is treated as persistent
+ * (offline, chunk deleted by a deploy) and falls through to the error UI
+ * instead of looping. It's longer than a cold boot on a slow mobile
+ * connection, so a reload that itself takes a while to boot can't loop; a
+ * fresh flake after the window gets its own reload.
+ */
+export const CHUNK_LOAD_RELOAD_GUARD_MS = 30_000
+
+const CHUNK_LOAD_ERROR_PATTERNS = [
+  // Chrome / Chromium
+  /Failed to fetch dynamically imported module/i,
+  // Firefox
+  /error loading dynamically imported module/i,
+  // Safari / WebKit (incl. every iOS browser); carries no URL
+  /Importing a module script failed/i,
+  // Vite's dynamic-import dependency preloader
+  /Unable to preload CSS/i,
+  // Next.js / webpack (JS and CSS chunks)
+  /Loading (CSS )?chunk [^\s]+ failed/i,
+]
+
+export function isChunkLoadError(error: unknown): boolean {
+  if (typeof error !== 'object' || error === null) return false
+
+  const name = 'name' in error && typeof error.name === 'string' ? error.name : ''
+  if (name === 'ChunkLoadError') return true
+
+  const message = 'message' in error && typeof error.message === 'string' ? error.message : ''
+  return CHUNK_LOAD_ERROR_PATTERNS.some((pattern) => pattern.test(message))
+}
+
+/**
+ * The guard is keyed on time, not on the error message: WebKit's message is
+ * identical for every chunk and sessionStorage outlives reloads, so a
+ * message-keyed guard (as in TanStack's `lazyRouteComponent`) only ever
+ * reloads once per tab.
+ */
+export function shouldReloadForChunkError({
+  now,
+  lastReloadAt,
+  guardMs = CHUNK_LOAD_RELOAD_GUARD_MS,
+}: {
+  now: number
+  lastReloadAt: number | null
+  guardMs?: number
+}): boolean {
+  if (lastReloadAt === null) return true
+  // A timestamp in the future means the clock moved backwards; don't trust it
+  if (lastReloadAt > now) return false
+  return now - lastReloadAt >= guardMs
+}
+
+type ChunkReloadStorage = Pick<Storage, 'getItem' | 'setItem'>
+
+/**
+ * Returns `undefined` when there's no usable value, and `null` when storage
+ * itself can't be read (private mode, blocked site data, SSR).
+ */
+function readLastReloadAt(storage: ChunkReloadStorage): number | undefined | null {
+  try {
+    const raw = storage.getItem(CHUNK_LOAD_RELOAD_STORAGE_KEY)
+    if (raw === null) return undefined
+    const value = Number(raw)
+    return Number.isFinite(value) ? value : undefined
+  } catch {
+    return null
+  }
+}
+
+function writeLastReloadAt(storage: ChunkReloadStorage, now: number): boolean {
+  try {
+    storage.setItem(CHUNK_LOAD_RELOAD_STORAGE_KEY, String(now))
+    return true
+  } catch {
+    return false
+  }
+}
+
+function getSessionStorage(): ChunkReloadStorage | undefined {
+  if (typeof window === 'undefined') return undefined
+  try {
+    return window.sessionStorage
+  } catch {
+    return undefined
+  }
+}
+
+/**
+ * Decides whether `error` should trigger a page reload, recording the reload
+ * in the guard when it should. Without a working storage there's no loop
+ * guard, so it never reloads.
+ */
+export function claimChunkLoadReload(
+  error: unknown,
+  {
+    storage = getSessionStorage(),
+    now = Date.now(),
+  }: { storage?: ChunkReloadStorage; now?: number } = {}
+): boolean {
+  if (!storage || !isChunkLoadError(error)) return false
+
+  const lastReloadAt = readLastReloadAt(storage)
+  if (lastReloadAt === null) return false
+  if (!shouldReloadForChunkError({ now, lastReloadAt: lastReloadAt ?? null })) return false
+
+  return writeLastReloadAt(storage, now)
+}
+
+const decisions = new WeakMap<object, boolean>()
+
+/**

+ * `onError` handler (commit) can both ask and get the same answer while the
+ * guard is only claimed once.
+ */
+export function getChunkLoadReloadDecision(error: unknown): boolean {
+  if (typeof error !== 'object' || error === null) return false
+
+  const cached = decisions.get(error)
+  if (cached !== undefined) return cached
+
+  const decision = claimChunkLoadReload(error)
+  decisions.set(error, decision)
+  return decision

issue.title: fix(studio): stop queued nuqs writes undoing redirects on TanStack
issue.body:
On TanStack, a full load (or reload) of the Table Editor index with a table in history bounced back to the table list instead of opening the last table. A nuqs write queued in the same commit as the redirect (the sidebar provider's no-op `?sidebar=` clear on mount) flushed on the next tick, and Studio's TanStack adapter replaced the URL using the render-time pathname (`/editor`), undoing the redirect. Master has since stopped the sidebar provider making that write, but any other queued write could still undo a redirect the same way. Reproduced on master at the time (TanStack only, the Next adapter isn't affected); found while testing #51067.

Also, on both runtimes, the index pushed the last table on top of itself, so Back landed on the index and redirected again (to the table's saved schema), wiping Forward.

**Changed:**
- `nuqs-tanstack-adapter`: read the pathname from `router.latestLocation` when nuqs flushes (it already builds `search` from the live URL). Queued writes now apply to wherever the user is at flush time, rather than the page that queued them.
- Table Editor index: redirect with `replace` instead of `push`, so the index never stays in history.

**Added:**
- Real-TanStack-router adapter test (queued write + navigation in the same commit); fails without the fix.
- Sidebar provider tests: no URL write on mount, and `?sidebar=` is cleared when the sidebar closes. These guard master's provider behavior.
- Table Editor index page test for the `replace` redirects.

## To test (TanStack Studio, plus the Back case on Next)

- Open a table, then full-load `/project/<ref>/editor` and reload on it – lands on the last table
- Table Editor nav link from another page still opens the last table
- From another page, open the Table Editor, change schema a couple of times, then Back – returns to the previous page (not the table in `public`), and Forward still works
- Open/close sidebars (Advisor Center, AI Assistant), switch schema in the Table Editor, open/close an auth provider panel – URL params update as before, Back/Forward work

issue.title: fix(studio): push history when opening url-driven panels
issue.body: Opening a URL-driven panel pushes a history entry. Close goes back only when this session still owns that entry and the rest of the URL is unchanged. A panel back records its destination URL, and the page-level unsaved-changes guard skips its confirm only for that URL. Scripted `navigation.back` isn't treated as a user back. Forward that restores an id this session just deleted clears it with no toast, and any other missing id is still the normal not-found case. **Changed:** - Panel open still pushes. Close, Cancel, and a successful save go back when this session owns the entry. A clear that doesn't own the entry replaces, and a second clear of an already-clear key does nothing. - A new value while the same panel is already open replaces, even when the caller passes push. Search and other non-panel query updates stay replace. - A missing delete id is always replaced. The id from the successful delete is cleared with no toast. Any other missing id is replaced and shows the existing not-found toast, even while that mutation is still successful. Roles, vault secrets, OAuth apps, functions, triggers, indexes, wrappers, vector tables, cron jobs, enumerated types, webhooks, and edge function secrets share that helper. - Next `routeChangeStart` and TanStack traversals (`BACK`, `FORWARD`, `GO`) skip the unsaved-changes confirm only when the destination is the URL recorded for that panel back. Push and replace still confirm. - Scripted `navigation.back` is `userInitiated: false`. Aborted `committed` and `finished` promises are caught. - The restore `popstate` listener only exists while a canceled dirty back is being put back, and it's removed when that restore finishes, times out, or a real traverse cancels it. If the restore never lands, the swallowed popstate is dispatched again so the address bar and the panel state match. - The Next router binding is removed when the guard unmounts, so a later navigation can clear the pending destination. - Creating a queue uses `router.replace` onto the queue page, so it replaces the `?new=true` entry and history is the list, then the queue. The queue name is encoded in the path. - `useAddonsPagePanel` uses `usePanelQueryState` with `parseAsStringLiteral`. The add-on `commitPanel` helper is gone and those side panels call `closePanel`. Webhook save uses `handleCommit`, and the webhook form still resets from the effect that runs when the panel opens. **Added:** - A dirty page doesn't confirm again when a panel back starts a Next route change to the recorded URL, and a different route still declines. A TanStack push is still blocked while a panel destination is pending. - Roles delete: `history.forward()` restores `delete=`, then the stale-id replace clears it. After that delete, a different missing id is cleared and toasts "Role cannot be found". - Webhooks: `history.forward()` restores `delete=`, then the stale-id replace clears it with no "Webhook not found" toast. - Queue create: success replaces the create-sheet entry, and the path encodes the queue name. ## To test 1. Database → Roles, Add role. The URL gains `?new=true`. Back closes the panel and stays on the page, and Forward reopens it. Repeat on Next and TanStack. 2. On a dirty page, closing the panel doesn't raise the page-level unsaved-changes dialog. A link to another page, or a browser Back that leaves the page, still does. 3. Delete a vault secret, a custom role, an enumerated type, a webhook, or an edge function secret, then Forward. The delete dialog doesn't stay on the deleted id, and there's no not-found toast for that id. 4. After that delete, open `?delete=` for a different id that isn't in the list. The param is cleared and the not-found toast shows. 5. Create a queue. The queue page opens in place of `?new=true`, and Back returns to the queue list without reopening the create sheet. 6. On a dirty webhook, Back still asks to discard. 7. Type in a list search. The URL updates in place, and Back doesn't undo each keystroke.

issue.title: fix(ui-patterns): only initiate the command menu when it opens
issue.body: Closing the command menu called `setOpen(false)`, and `setOpen` always ran `init()`, which mounts the lazy `CommandMenu`. So the first close (e.g. a shallow `routeChangeComplete` from switching schema in the Table Editor on Next, or the load-time `onResolved` on TanStack) mounted the menu and its hooks fetched api keys, project settings, the projects list, secrets, auth/storage config and integrations. Reproduces on master, found while testing #52016. The menu and its queries now load on first open instead (on TanStack that used to happen at page load). **Changed:** - `viewState.ts` – `setOpen` only calls `init()` when opening - `CommandProvider.tsx` – add `completeNavigation` to the listener effect deps - `SqlEditor.Commands.tsx` – treat mounting while open as just opened, so the first Cmd+K still prefetches tables **Added:** - `viewState.test.ts` – closing doesn't initiate a never-opened menu, opening does - `CommandProvider.navigation.test.tsx` – a real or shallow completion leaves a never-opened menu unmounted and closes an open one. Fails without the fix. - `SqlEditor.Commands.test.tsx` – mounting while open prefetches tables ## To test - Table Editor, open DevTools Network, switch schema (e.g. public to auth) – only the schema's pg-meta queries fire, no api-keys, settings, projects or integrations requests - Load a project and navigate via the sidebar before opening Cmd+K – none of those requests - Cmd+K – the menu opens, its commands work, and the first open fetches tables - Navigate via a command – the menu closes - With the menu open, follow a shallow path change (e.g. open another SQL snippet) – the menu closes - Repeat locally on TanStack (`pnpm dev:studio`)

issue.title: fix(studio): stop queued nuqs writes undoing redirects on TanStack
issue.body:
On TanStack, a full load (or reload) of the Table Editor index with a table in history bounced back to the table list instead of opening the last table. A nuqs write queued in the same commit as the redirect (the sidebar provider's no-op `?sidebar=` clear on mount) flushed on the next tick, and Studio's TanStack adapter replaced the URL using the render-time pathname (`/editor`), undoing the redirect. Master has since stopped the sidebar provider making that write, but any other queued write could still undo a redirect the same way. Reproduced on master at the time (TanStack only, the Next adapter isn't affected); found while testing #51067.

Also, on both runtimes, the index pushed the last table on top of itself, so Back landed on the index and redirected again (to the table's saved schema), wiping Forward.

**Changed:**
- `nuqs-tanstack-adapter`: read the pathname from `router.latestLocation` when nuqs flushes (it already builds `search` from the live URL). Queued writes now apply to wherever the user is at flush time, rather than the page that queued them.
- Table Editor index: redirect with `replace` instead of `push`, so the index never stays in history.

**Added:**
- Real-TanStack-router adapter test (queued write + navigation in the same commit); fails without the fix.
- Sidebar provider tests: no URL write on mount, and `?sidebar=` is cleared when the sidebar closes. These guard master's provider behavior.
- Table Editor index page test for the `replace` redirects.

## To test (TanStack Studio, plus the Back case on Next)

- Open a table, then full-load `/project/<ref>/editor` and reload on it – lands on the last table
- Table Editor nav link from another page still opens the last table
- From another page, open the Table Editor, change schema a couple of times, then Back – returns to the previous page (not the table in `public`), and Forward still works
- Open/close sidebars (Advisor Center, AI Assistant), switch schema in the Table Editor, open/close an auth provider panel – URL params update as before, Back/Forward work

issue.title: ci(studio-e2e): reserve supabase ports from the ephemeral range
issue.body: About a quarter of failed self-hosted Studio E2E runs in the last two weeks die at "Start supabase" (`supabase start --exclude studio,mailpit --workdir ./e2e/studio`) with `address already in use` binding `0.0.0.0:54322`, in a single shard, on both next and tanstack. The local ports in `e2e/studio/supabase/config.toml` sit inside Linux's ephemeral range, so an outbound connection during the image pull can take 54322; `ss -tlnp` only lists listeners, which is why diagnostics reported the port free. This reserves `54320-54329` before installs and image pulls, keeping any ports already reserved, and snapshots sockets on that range when `supabase start` fails. Follows up the diagnostics from #45637 and #46607. **Changed:** - `.github/workflows/studio-e2e-test.yml` – append `54320-54329` to `net.ipv4.ip_local_reserved_ports` before dependency install, Playwright install, and image pulls, so an outbound connect cannot occupy them and any ports the runner already reserved stay reserved. - `.github/workflows/studio-e2e-test.yml` – when `supabase start` fails, snapshot TCP sockets on `54320-54329` immediately, before the build finishes and a short-lived socket from the image pull is gone. - `.github/workflows/studio-e2e-test.yml` – pre-start diagnostics print the ephemeral port range and sockets on `54320-54329`; failure diagnostics use the same filter and group the last 300 log lines per container. ## To test - [x] "Reserve Supabase local ports" step prints `54320-54329` on every E2E shard - [x] All Studio E2E shards pass on next and tanstack - [ ] (on a future failure) the Start supabase step lists any socket on 54320-54329
